title: How ABS Keeps You Steering in a Panic Stop 🛑⚡ #shorts

scenes.text: Slam the brakes on ice, the wheels lock, and your steering does nothing.
A locked tire slides instead of rolling, and a sliding tire can't grip sideways to turn.
So every wheel gets a speed sensor. If one slows much faster than the car, a computer knows it's about to lock.
Valves cut that wheel's brake pressure, let it spin up, then squeeze again. Bosch says up to forty times a second.
Mercedes and Bosch first offered it in late nineteen seventy-eight.
A buzzing pedal means it's working. Don't pump. Press hard and steer. Many EVs even cut regen so the motor doesn't fight it.
On loose gravel, ABS can stop you longer. It trades distance for steering. Worth it? Follow EV Drive.
